appraisal_events.evidence: "Mais elle vous adore ! ... c'est lui qui saurait vous dire si c'est authentique ou non. Il n'y a personne comme lui pour ça." ... "tout ce que nous lui disons ne pèserait pas lourd auprès de ce que lui dirait Swann."
appraisal_events.explanation: Via Mme Cottard's doubly-reported account, Odette is said to adore Swann and prize his taste above all, and Mme Verdurin concedes his opinion outweighs the whole Verdurin circle's; the layered, flattery-tinged retelling counsels a conservative reading rather than full narrator endorsement.

appraisal_events.evidence: "je ne vous dis pas cela pour vous flatter, vous avez là une vraie amie comme on n'en a pas beaucoup"
appraisal_events.explanation: Distinct from her role as the reported source of the devotion that elevates Swann, Odette herself is directly praised by Mme Cottard as a rare, genuine friend; the sincerity is reported without explicit narrator endorsement of its objective truth.

status_effects.explanation: Reported adoration and prized judgment mildly elevate Swann's local standing, tempered by the layered, self-interested reporting through which the claim arrives.

Being singled out by Mme Cottard as an unusually devoted and genuine friend modestly raises Odette's local standing, though the claim rests on Mme Cottard's sincerity rather than narratorial confirmation.

ambiguities: The praise of Swann and Odette arrives entirely through Mme Cottard's retelling of a prior conversation (itself embedded with quotations from Odette and Mme Verdurin), and the surrounding detail of Mme Cottard's social vanity (aigrette, monogrammed cardholder) leaves open how much of this flattering picture is accurate versus performed for Swann's benefit.

M. Verdurin, Mme Verdurin, comte de Forcheville, and le peintre appear only as incidental figures in reported speech or a passing biographical detail (an evening at the painter's with Forcheville), with no distinct local evaluative outcome of their own, so they were not scored.
